VibePascal v56 -- arm-linux native compiler (32-bit ARM, ARMHF/EABIHF; a 32-bit
Raspberry Pi OS is the target this exists for).  An inferred inline var
initialised from a real constant is a Double, whatever the constant's value
happens to be.
Source commit: a187bbac34 (merge of inlinevar-real-default)
Compiler fix:  f06e46d8eb  (compiler/pstatmnt.pas, compiler/defutil.pas, compiler/ncnv.pas)
Parent release: v55 (eae5d3e919a26a7db19937da10da1c8b610b17da)
Built: 2026-09-10, cross-built on x86_64-linux via a freshly bootstrapped
       compiler/ppcrossarm.v56hf (from a187bbac34, -dFPC_ARMHF,
       BINUTILSPREFIX=arm-linux-gnueabihf-)
Binary: bin/ppcarm  md5 d9fd3cb9503e86206e2fdf456b62c61a
                    sha256 5b1bdf1e7fe57c57adb4c75dea5e051a5b0857e11ee0a2ad5d60abd635a64a92

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  Only compiler/{pstatmnt,defutil,ncnv}.pas changed between
v55 and v56: no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format change.  Pair it
with the existing vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units.tar.gz, which stays valid and
is still REQUIRED -- this is a bin-only refresh, not a standalone install.

ABI: ARMHF (EABIHF), hard float.  The compiler tree defaults to FPC_ARMEL, so
this build passes -dFPC_ARMHF explicitly at BOTH stages -- the host cross
compiler and the native one.  Building the cross stage without it produces an
ARMEL compiler that cannot even read this tree's ARMHF system.ppu ("Can't find
unit system"), which is what that error means if you hit it.

WHAT CHANGED
  An inline var with no type annotation used to take its type from the real
  constant you initialised it with, and that type changes with the VALUE:

      var a := 1.0;      // Single   -  4 bytes,  7 digits
      var b := 0.1;      // Extended - 10 bytes, 19 digits
      var d := 1/2;      // Double

  v56 infers the DEFAULT real type -- Double -- in either direction.  RANGE is
  never traded: 1.0e400 and 1.0e-4000 keep their wider type.  A variable or
  non-constant expression keeps its own type, and an explicit `single(1.0)`
  still wins.  How real CONSTANTS themselves are typed is NOT touched.

VERIFIED ON THIS PLATFORM BY EXECUTION, NOT BY INSPECTION
  The COMPILER is a 32-bit ARM binary run under qemu-arm-static on the build
  host, and every program it produced was RUN too, not merely linked.

  A/B against the PUBLISHED v55 arm binary (md5 494305fbcdbc4e156a7357fe0940d573,
  taken out of its own shipped tarball and md5-checked against that tarball's
  VERSION.txt before it was trusted as a control):

    tinlinevarrealinfer1.pp, three modes -- mode is a real axis of this fix
      -Munleashed        v55 52 checks / 25 fails  ->  v56 52 / 0
      -Mdelphi           v55 49 checks / 16 fails  ->  v56 49 / 0
      -Mdelphiunicode    v55 49 checks / 16 fails  ->  v56 49 / 0
    The control FAILS in every mode, so a pass cannot be reached by accident.

    tinlinevarrealinfer2.pp is a %FAIL test -- `for var i := 1.0` must stay
    rejected.  BOTH compilers reject it with "Ordinal expression expected" and
    zero internal errors.

  NO REGRESSION, also by execution on the v56 compiler:
    tinlinevarnativeint1.pp   45/45, NativeInt=4  (32-bit: the whole point of
                                                   the v54 NativeInt rule)
    tinlinevarstrinfer1.pp    PASS
    tblockscopefinal1.pp      PASS -- every corner released EXACTLY ONCE
                              (kills counted, so a double-free scores as a fail)
    tinlinevar2 / tinlinevar3 both still correctly REJECTED

  LIMIT, stated plainly: qemu-user is an emulator.  It runs the real shipped
  bytes and real ARM encodings, so codegen and RTL defects DO surface -- but it
  is not a Raspberry Pi.  NOBODY HAS RUN THIS ON PHYSICAL ARM HARDWARE.
  Re-runnable: sh dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh
